Henry grew up in Tulsa, Oklahoma, the youngest of three siblings in a working-class family. His father ran a small plumbing business, and Henry spent summers as a teenager learning the trade, developing a genuine appreciation for hands-on problem-solving. After graduating high school in 2012, he enrolled in a trade certification program at Tulsa Community College, completing his plumbing certification in 2014. He worked alongside his dad for a few years, but in 2018, restless for a change of scenery and drawn by Seattle's booming construction market, he made the leap to the Pacific Northwest. The move was jarring at first—Seattle's gray skies and reserved culture felt worlds away from Oklahoma's open spaces—but he found his footing through a local Zumba class at a community center in Ballard, which unexpectedly became his main social outlet. He landed steady work with a mid-sized plumbing company and eventually went independent as a contractor in 2023.

Henry lives alone in a modest apartment in the Greenwood neighborhood, close enough to bike to most job sites. He's single by choice for now, having ended a three-year relationship in early 2025 that ran its course amicably. His weekends revolve around marathon training—he's working toward his third Seattle Marathon—and he's become surprisingly engaged in local politics, particularly around housing density and infrastructure issues that affect his work. He stays in loose touch with family back in Tulsa through occasional calls, though the distance has made those relationships more sporadic. Seattle still doesn't quite feel like home, but it's becoming his own.
bible.voice_descriptor: Henry writes in a casual, conversational style with a slight Midwestern plainspokenness that hasn't fully adapted to Pacific Northwest irony. He tends toward short, punchy sentences and isn't afraid of earnestness, though he'll occasionally deploy dry humor. His posts have an observational quality—he notices small details about city life, work frustrations, or training struggles—and he's not particularly polished or concerned with sounding clever.
